title: Customer Insights - Journeys: Outreach Optimization Agent picks email send times
summary: Hold for corrections to the enablement route and spending-control guidance. The AI Hub route omits Settings, and Microsoft already directs administrators to consumption limits for this agent rather than leaving their applicability unconfirmed. The roadmap facts and the main preview behaviour are supported.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Outreach Optimization Agent is an AI journey step that chooses marketing email send times.
claims.quote: Outreach Optimization Agent is an AI-powered journey step in Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Journeys that optimizes when your marketing emails are sent.

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: A maker adds the step to a journey and selects one or more emails for it to schedule.
claims.quote: You add Outreach Optimization Agent to a customer journey like any other step, and the agent handles scheduling from there. When configuring the step, select one or more email messages.

claims.where: What's changing: second paragraph; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The agent reads aggregated historical email interaction data, including opens and clicks, to find high-engagement send times.
claims.quote: It accesses your organization's historical interaction data, such as when past emails were opened or clicked, to identify general patterns of peak engagement across your audience.

claims.claim: The agent uses a generic fallback strategy when historical engagement data is unavailable.
claims.quote: If historical engagement data isn't yet available (for example, for a first-time user), the agent uses a generic fallback strategy

claims.claim: All emails sent is a goal option for a multi-email sequence.
claims.quote: All emails are sent: The goal is met when the agent has delivered every email in the sequence.

claims.claim: Any link clicked is a goal option for a multi-email sequence.
claims.quote: Any link in any email is clicked: The goal is met as soon as the contact clicks any link in any of the emails in the sequence.

claims.claim: Selected links clicked is a goal option for a multi-email sequence.
claims.quote: Selected links are clicked: The goal is met when the contact clicks one of the specific links you designate across the emails.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The configured end date bounds when the agent can send the selected emails.
claims.quote: The end date defines the latest point in time by which the agent can send emails. The agent schedules all selected emails at optimal times, but ensures that all sends occur before this date.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The preview agent page says remaining emails are sent even if the sequence goal is met early.
claims.quote: If the goal is met before all emails have been sent, the agent continues to send the remaining emails in the sequence. It doesn't cancel queued messages.

claims.claim: The agent records the goal as met at the point it is achieved.
claims.quote: it records the goal as achieved at the point the condition was satisfied

claims.claim: The AI Hub page describes using engagement history and real-time signals to adjust timing, frequency and follow-up behaviour.
claims.quote: It analyzes engagement history and real-time signals to adjust message timing, frequency, and follow-up behavior.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions

claims.quote: Searched: Outreach Optimization Agent rollout generally available enable default; read the agent page in full, including multi-email sequences and goal evaluation. It documents continuing queued sends, not early exit.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: Outreach Optimization Agent identity audit approval sends; Outreach Optimization Agent audit identity. Read agent, AI Hub and responsible AI FAQ pages; none identifies its runtime sending identity.

claims.quote: Searched: Outreach Optimization Agent audit identity; Outreach Optimization Agent identity audit approval sends. Read agent, AI Hub and responsible AI FAQ pages; no send-time decision audit location is documented.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; controls[4].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Configured quiet times apply to this agent.
claims.quote: The agent respects your organization's configured quiet times. Even if historical data suggests a high-engagement window outside permitted hours (for example, late at night), the agent won't schedule emails during quiet-time periods.

claims.claim: The agent honours contact point consent.
claims.quote: The agent respects the communication preferences set for each contact or lead. If a contact has opted out of email communication on a specific address, no email is sent to that address.

claims.claim: Quiet times can apply for up to 21 consecutive days.
claims.quote: Quiet times can apply for up to 21 consecutive days. The combined quiet times effect (both quiet dates and quiet hours) must stay within the 21 day maximum.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout

claims.quote: If any mandatory prerequisite is no longer accepted in the Power Platform Admin Center: All enabled agents are automatically disabled. Agents remain unavailable until the prerequisite is accepted again.

claims.claim: Disabling AI agents at tenant level immediately disables all active Journeys agents.

claims.claim: Rollout mechanics beyond the preview are not described.
claims.quote: Searched: Outreach Optimization Agent rollout generally available enable default. Read the roadmap record and agent, AI Hub, prerequisites and FAQ pages; no post-preview rollout mechanics are given.

claims.claim: Manage Copilot Credits is reached through Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Copilot Credits.

claims.fix: Include the omitted heading: 'Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits'.

claims.claim: PUT /licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 sets the environment's MCSMessages allocation and TenantPool enforcement rule using the printed body properties.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are represented by the entitlement ID MCSMessages and are managed through the licensing/allocationsV2 operations of the Power Platform API. All programmatic examples in this article use API version 2024-10-01.
claims.fix: Set the call to 'PUT /licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01'. In its note add: 'The request body identifies scope.environmentId, sets allocatedEntitlements[].entitlementId to MCSMessages and allocation.quantity to the allocation, and sets enforcementRules[].ruleType to TenantPool with enabled false to disable tenant-pool draw.'

claims.claim: The capacity API host is https://api.powerplatform.com.
claims.quote: $apiBaseUrl = "https://api.powerplatform.com"

claims.claim: Disabling TenantPool draw does not disable every overage source.
claims.quote: Select Draw from the available capacity in my tenant to let the environment use unallocated prepaid capacity from the tenant pool. Select Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan to let the environment continue usage through the selected billing plan.

claims.claim: An environment-group rule can lock tenant-pool draw and cause updates to fail with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.claim: Move data across regions is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Generative AI features > Edit > Move data across regions.
claims.quote: select Manage. Select Environments. On the Environments page, select the target environment. In the environment details page, locate the Generative AI features card and select Edit. Select the Move data across regions checkbox.

claims.claim: Set-PowerPlatformGenerativeAiSettings -EnvironmentName <environment ID> -CrossGeoDataMovement $true allows cross-geography data movement for the environment.
claims.quote: Set-PowerPlatformGenerativeAiSettings -EnvironmentName <String> [-CrossGeoDataMovement <Boolean>] [-BingSearch <Boolean>] [-Microsoft365Services <Boolean>] [-ApiVersion <String>]. -CrossGeoDataMovement: Enables or disables cross-geo data movement.

claims.claim: The Move data across regions checkbox may be absent in regions with full in-region capacity.
claims.quote: If your environment is in a region that has full in-region capacity, the Move data across regions checkbox doesn't appear.

claims.claim: Quiet times is at Customer Insights - Journeys > Settings > Customer engagement > Quiet times.
claims.quote: To set up quiet times, go to Settings > Customer engagement > Quiet times.

claims.where: controls[4].api; controls[4].note; Governance controls table and closing paragraph
claims.claim: POST to the msdynmkt_quiettimesettings entity set creates a Quiet Time Setting record using caller-supplied configuration.
claims.quote: Create: POST /msdynmkt_quiettimesettings. EntitySetName: msdynmkt_quiettimesettings. Writable columns/attributes: msdynmkt_commercialdates, msdynmkt_commercialweeklyhours, msdynmkt_transactionaldates, msdynmkt_transactionalweeklyhours.
claims.fix: Set the call to 'POST /msdynmkt_quiettimesettings', removing the header and body description. Add to the note: 'The request body supplies quiet-time configuration through msdynmkt_commercialdates, msdynmkt_commercialweeklyhours, msdynmkt_transactionaldates and msdynmkt_transactionalweeklyhours as applicable.' Keep the existing qualification that this creates a general Quiet Time Setting record.

claims.claim: AI prompts is configured on the environment's Settings > Product > Features page.
claims.quote: In the admin center, select Environments > [select an environment] > Settings > Product > Features. On the Features settings page under AI Builder, enable the AI prompts toggle.
claims.fix: Complete the printed path as 'Power Platform admin center > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > AI Builder > AI prompts'.

claims.claim: An environment-group AI prompts rule can govern AI prompts availability.
claims.quote: If your environment is part of an environment group, you can also govern the AI prompts feature availability through the AI prompts environment group rule.

claims.claim: The Generative AI settings environment rule can control Move data across regions at scale.
claims.quote: Is it possible to modify the "Move data across regions" checkbox at scale across all my environments? Yes, you can use the Generative AI settings environment rule to control this at scale.

claims.claim: Capacity API changes require Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or equivalent licensing and capacity permissions.
claims.quote: Permission to manage licensing and capacity. Sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly show whether this named agent appears in the monthly credit-limit page's inventory.
claims.quote: Searched: Outreach Optimization Agent credits rate monthly limit. Read AI Hub setup and Manage Copilot Credits and capacity, including Manage monthly consumption limits; no inventory example explicitly names Outreach Optimization Agent.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed whether the per-agent monthly credit-limit control applies to this agent.
claims.quote: Steps to set up Outreach Optimization Agent: To control agent usage, configure message consumption limits. For more information, see Manage capacity.
claims.fix: Remove the final Open questions bullet. Replace the uncertainty with the narrower documented statement: 'AI Hub directs administrators to configure message consumption limits for Outreach Optimization Agent using the Copilot Studio capacity page.' Both https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/customer-insights/journeys/ai-hub and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-copilot-studio-messages-capacity are already cited. Do not equate the separate uncertainty about an inventory example with an absence of applicability guidance.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio licensing reports and environment capacity status can be used to review credit consumption.
claims.quote: Administrators can view capacity and consumption data at the environment and agent level, and can download consumption reports by environment, agent, or user.

claims.claim: Linking quiet times to the compliance profile used by journey messages makes those messages respect the configured quiet times.
claims.quote: Once a quiet time has been added to a compliance profile, all messages designated with that compliance profile respect the quiet times configured.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The governance checklist's controls are all represented by rows in the controls table.
claims.quote: Re-check the prerequisites after any change to data movement or AI prompts settings. The five rows cover agent availability, agent enablement, capacity, data movement and quiet times, but not AI prompts.
claims.fix: Narrow that After rollout bullet to: 'Re-check the Move data across regions prerequisite after changing data movement settings, because losing a mandatory prerequisite disables all enabled agents.' The At rollout bullet may continue to refer to accepting prerequisites as part of enabling the agent.
